title: Julio Escolano — A Practical Guide to Public Debt Dynamics, Fiscal Sustainability, and Cyclical Adjustment of Budgetary Aggregates (IMF Technical Notes and Manuals 10/02, January 2010)
use: Exact debt/GDP accounting and the distinction between constant ratios, stability and explicit terminal financing restrictions; no historical estimates imported.
verification: Actual official PDF downloaded and text inspected: printed pp1–5 (scope exclusions, notation, exact interest/growth factors, recursive dynamics and stationary balance); pp7–8 (bounded ratios, explicit discounted terminal-debt condition and associated PV identity). Source is an author technical note, not a claim of IMF institutional policy. Some extracted formula typography is imperfect; chapter equations and synthetic counterexamples independently derived from dated cash flows. No claim of complete-document or current empirical verification.

title: Congressional Budget Office — Effects of Automatic Stabilizers on the Federal Budget: 2026 to 2036 (August 2026)
use: Methodological distinction between automatic budget responses and discretionary fiscal action, and limitations of cyclical adjustment; no projection figures used.
verification: Actual official HTML body inspected: automatic revenue/outlay responses, potential-output and unemployment gaps, and cyclically adjusted deficit limitations. Report baseline is February2026, with specified late2025 policy/economic cutoffs; it is not October2026 observed data. Chapter cites only the methodological discussion and creates its own synthetic calculations.

title: Eric Sims, University of Notre Dame — Lecture 11: Debt, Taxes, and Ricardian Equivalence, ECON 30020 (Spring 2026)
use: Primary two-date teaching reference for household and government PV budgets and conditional financing neutrality.
verification: Actual20-page official faculty PDF opened and inspected: slides4–13, government/household period budgets, terminal condition, lifetime taxes and Ricardian assumptions; slides16–20 inspected for distinction between a fixed-rate desired-demand calculation and fixed-endowment equilibrium. Chapter uses original partial-equilibrium household values with explicit credit counterparties, and independently derives a separate short-run multiplier model. No wholesale copying or unsupported assertion of general neutrality.
